title: the-buildme-gates-guard-a-crossing-not-a-state
intention: The two gates that guard BUILDME — `buildme_rides_the_chart` and `buildme_rides_the_intent` — hold jurisdiction over a build that HAPPENED, not only over the act of crossing into it, so a voyage cannot skip them by opening its journal with the cursor already past BUILDME.
why:
MEASURED 2026-08-14, twice: once against the live corpus, once by running the gate both ways over the same input.

THE GATE'S JURISDICTION IS A CROSSING. `transitions.py:1423` reads `if target == "BUILDME" and target_idx > wf.cursor:` — the entry gate fires when, and only when, the move being journaled lands ON BUILDME. Its siblings sit the same way: the build gate keys off `wf.here == "PROVEME"`, the exit gate off `target == "PROVED"`. For every other gate that is exactly right, because the thing each guards IS a crossing. For the entry gate it is not, because the thing it guards is that A BUILD WAS CHARTED — and a build is a period, not an edge.

THE A/B THAT PROVES IT. One cast ticket with no berthed chart chain (`constrain-floor-authors-and-provenance-is-measured`), two emits, scratch history paths:

  A. `[TICKETME] -> BUILDME`   REFUSED EntryGateRed — 'no berthed chart chain claims ticket ... the build has no charted course'. Nothing journaled.
  B. `[BUILDME] -> PROVEME`    PASSED. Three checks proved — the_target_is_in_the_vocabulary, the_crossing_moves_the_cursor, the_crossing_is_a_legal_edge. `entry_gate` field: null.

Same ticket. Same missing chain. The difference is entirely which edge the journal opened on, and the second route is one keystroke of the workflow string away from the first.

AND IT IS NOT HYPOTHETICAL — IT WAS WALKED TODAY. `cairn/devices/builder/machines/orient/history.json` seq 0, at 2026-08-14, is `THINKME -> TICKETME -> BUILDME -> [PROVEME:waiting] -> ...`, ticket `orient-floor-authors-and-provenance-is-measured`, three checks proved, `entry_gate: null`. That ticket has NO berthed chart chain (grep over every packet in `~/.cairn/devices/chart/` for its id returns nothing) and NO intent berth (`intent_berth: None`) — and it stands at PROVED. Both BUILDME gates were owed and neither was paid, and the record of the voyage is clean because nothing ever asked.

THE LIVED SYMPTOM: a reader looking at orient's history sees a complete, well-formed voyage with every check it was asked for passing. The absence is invisible at the surface where it matters, because a gate that never ran leaves no trace of not running — the `entry_gate` field is null for 'exempt', null for 'not applicable', and null for 'never asked'. That is the same class of failure as the 2026-07-24 'done' reported while the files stood unmoved: not a lie, a question nobody put.
traces_to: Law 4 — a rule that matters is enforced by physics, not policy. The chart requirement IS physics on one edge and policy everywhere else on the same path, which means it is policy.
Law 8 — nothing enters proven-space without a proof a hollow build couldn't pass. A build whose preamble was never run is the hollow shape the chain exists to refuse, and it reached PROVED.
Law 3 — nothing is known until measured. That the gate covered BUILDME was assumed for as long as it has existed; two emits said otherwise.
Akien 2026-08-14 — 'we keep on until this whole skills and mechanical workflow is solid'. This is the workflow's own floor with a door in it.

falsifier.proves_green: (1) THE PREDICATE IS ABOUT THE BUILD, NOT THE EDGE. Whatever ships must be able to answer 'was this component's build charted?' at a crossing that is not the BUILDME edge — the natural place is the same crossing the build gate already owns (leaving PROVEME), because that is the first moment the system is told a build finished. (2) A JOURNAL MAY STILL OPEN MID-PATH. See the owner clause: four legitimate cases exist and a fix that reds them has traded one false reading for four. The distinction the repair must draw is pre-gate-component vs skipped-gate, and it is drawable — the four carry zero checks and predate the gate's ticket. (3) NULL MUST STOP MEANING THREE THINGS. `entry_gate: null` currently reads as exempt, not-applicable, and never-asked. A record of truth that cannot distinguish 'this gate passed you' from 'this gate never saw you' is Law 7's collapse at a diagnostic surface. (4) NO RETROACTIVE JUDGEMENT OF SEALED VOYAGES without Akien's ruling — see `the_question_that_rides_along`.
falsifier.proves_red: DONE when the A/B above is re-run and route B refuses for the same reason route A does, AND the four pre-gate journals still stand unred under a full shake, AND `entry_gate` distinguishes never-asked from passed in the record. WRONG INTENT if: (1) a journal is forbidden from opening mid-path — that reds four legitimate histories to close one hole; (2) the gate is moved to fire on EVERY crossing, which asks a chart of a back-edge retreat and makes a kick-back impossible, the motion a red exists to produce; (3) orient's sealed PROVED is quietly re-opened or its record edited — history is append-only (Law 7) and what is owed there is a new record, not a corrected old one; (4) the fix ships and nothing measures it, given that the only reason this was found is that a build happened to be standing at the other edge.
falsifier.horizon: Small and it is one predicate moved, plus the null-collapse in the journal field. The part that is NOT one build is what to do about the voyage that already walked through — that is the question below, and it is Akien's.

how: Fix buildme_rides_the_chart and buildme_rides_the_intent to guard the BUILDME crossing (a build that happened), not just the at-rest state. The gate fires at the crossing event, not as a static check.
